title: AI beside the dispatcher
hook: Replace the dispatcher? No. Assist them.
message: Introduce ProfitLane to independent dispatchers; proposed AI system tracking and recommendation-score concepts support human judgment.
caption: Who makes the call at your dispatch desk? Angel’s answer is the starting point for ProfitLane. In development.
cta: Follow @profitlane.dispatch for practical conversations and honest product updates.

title: Your load-review routine
hook: What do you check before you even discuss the rate?
message: Listen to real workflows before choosing features.
caption: Every dispatcher has a first check. What is yours?
cta: Comment with one check, without sharing private load details.

title: The miles before the load
hook: Five hundred miles. From where?
message: Add deadhead to loaded miles before comparing revenue per mile.
caption: Fictional offer: $1,200, 500 loaded miles… plus the miles before pickup. What would you ask next?
cta: Comment with the first detail you would confirm before discussing the rate.

title: A better filming checklist
hook: A useful load video starts with clean inputs.
message: Use fictional load data and clear labels in educational content.
caption: No private rate confirmations needed to teach the basics.
cta: Which input would you explain first?

title: Revenue is not take-home pay
hook: Twelve hundred. How much stays?
message: Subtract relevant costs; revenue per mile alone is incomplete.
caption: The payment card says $1,200. What has it still got to cover? All numbers are fictional teaching inputs.
cta: Name one cost you would check before calling a remainder take-home pay.

title: Build the next cost checklist
hook: Which cost is easiest to leave out?
message: Include fuel, tolls, time and allocated operating costs.
caption: Help us build a more useful review checklist.
cta: Suggest one overlooked cost.

title: One week of questions
hook: What did this week leave unanswered?
message: Use audience questions to choose the next explanation.
caption: We are listening before adding more concepts.
cta: Leave a question for next week.

title: Angel and the mission
hook: Why build ProfitLane? To help dispatchers.
message: Angel introduces his dispatcher-first vision and an authentic explanation of what he would review; approve his approximately eight-year background wording before filming.
caption: A conversation with Angel about the purpose behind ProfitLane. Proposed assistance, with the dispatcher in control.
cta: Ask Angel one question you would want answered before exploring the product.

title: Prepare a rate conversation
hook: Before asking for more, organize the reason.
message: Use accurate route, timing and cost facts; no guaranteed negotiation outcome.
caption: Facts make a clearer conversation than a random counteroffer.
cta: Write down your three key facts.

title: Fuel math you can check
hook: How many gallons is this?
message: Total miles divided by assumed MPG, multiplied by fuel price, estimates fuel cost.
caption: Ten tokens, 100 hypothetical gallons. A fuel estimate is easier to check when the units stay visible.
cta: Save the method; which assumption would you check first?

title: What changes your fuel estimate?
hook: Would you use the same MPG for every trip?
message: Vehicle and route assumptions need review.
caption: One estimate cannot describe every truck or route.
cta: Tell us which assumption you revisit.

title: A score is a starting point
hook: Seventy-six. Would you take it?
message: Proposed 1–100 recommendation tool: weight relative to distance, pre-trip deadhead, diesel prices in relevant areas, pallet count and load payment; unvalidated, with no guaranteed outcome.
caption: Would you take it—or ask for the missing details? 76 is an arbitrary illustration, not a computed or validated recommendation.
cta: Tell Angel which missing input you would ask for first.

title: Design the explanation
hook: What does Angel mean by AI system tracking?
format: Casual founder Q&A with labeled concept cards
message: Explain the intended identification of logistics companies using AI in broker–dispatcher communication so dispatchers can choose whom to work with. Method, accuracy and availability remain unverified.
caption: AI system tracking: Angel’s proposed concept, not a working detection demonstration. Questions help shape a clearer explanation.
cta: Which part of this proposed concept would you want Angel to explain?

title: Your three-question review
hook: Which of these three checks comes first for you?
message: Invite audience priorities without presenting an acceptance rule.
caption: Miles, time or costs—where do you start?
cta: Comment with your order and why.

title: Ask before you counter
hook: Need an answer. Three questions first.
message: Clarify appointment times, accessorial terms and load details before negotiating.
caption: Fictional call and hypothetical amounts, not market-rate advice. Three questions, then a conditional counter. What would you add?
cta: Save the questions or comment with another detail you would clarify.

title: Time belongs in the review
hook: Two loads. Same miles. Different time commitments.
message: Pickup windows, waiting and delivery timing affect the review.
caption: Mileage does not tell the whole schedule. Fictional comparison.
cta: What timing detail do you always confirm?

title: The same rate, different trip
hook: A or B? Same payment.
message: Compare revenue across total miles while reviewing costs and time.
caption: A or B? Same fictional payment, different total miles—and still more questions before booking.
cta: Comment A, B, or need more information, and explain the question behind your choice.

title: Missing information matters
hook: What should an assistant do when an input is missing?
message: Flag unknown inputs instead of presenting certainty.
caption: Concept in development: unknown should stay unknown.
cta: Which missing input should trigger a follow-up?

title: Walk through the proposed assistant
hook: Paper prototype. Two different ideas.
message: Walk through the proposed load recommendation inputs and explain AI system tracking separately; concept-only visuals, no live detection, scoring or booking demonstration.
caption: Paper, not a product screen: two proposed ProfitLane concepts and the questions still open.
cta: Follow for confirmed product updates; real product-exploration and demo details will be shared only when approved and available.

title: Make labels readable
hook: Can you read the important part in two seconds?
message: Keep concept labels visible and explain assumptions in captions.
caption: Clear wording helps people understand what is real and what is proposed.
cta: Which part would you simplify?

title: Listen before the next batch
hook: What should we explain next: fuel, time or deadhead?
message: Let qualified questions shape future education.
caption: Choose a topic for the next recording session.
cta: Comment fuel, time or deadhead.

title: The dispatcher stays in control
hook: Quick answer? Pause the clock.
message: Angel explains how dispatcher experience and relationships guide decisions; AI system tracking and the score remain proposed assistance concepts.
caption: Fictional desk challenge: quick answer, or better questions? Angel pauses the clock.
cta: What information would make you pause before deciding?

title: Build a useful reply video
hook: A good question deserves more than a quick reply.
message: Answer a real question accurately; do not invent a customer comment.
caption: We are collecting questions for the next explanation.
cta: Ask one specific load-review question.

title: Three inputs to double-check
hook: Before trusting any summary, check the inputs.
message: Verify total miles, fuel assumptions and schedule; this is not a complete operating checklist.
caption: Better inputs help you ask better questions.
cta: Save these checks and add your own.

title: What a demo request should explain
hook: Before you request a demo, you should know what is available.
message: Plan a product-exploration and demo CTA only after Angel confirms the actual feature, demo and request route. No business contact details or availability are supplied.
caption: Product updates should tell you what you can really try.
cta: Now: follow for development updates. Later, after approval and verification: explore the features and request a demo through the real profile link.

title: Answer a real dispatcher question
hook: Let us work through one question from the dispatch desk.
format: Comment reply; use a genuine approved question
message: Use a real question with consent or label it as a team prompt.
caption: A practical explanation starts with a specific question.
cta: What would you like us to work through next?

title: Review useful responses
hook: Which explanation helped you ask a better question?
message: Measure useful audience feedback without fabricating testimonials.
caption: Your feedback helps shape the next month of education.
cta: Name a topic we should revisit.

title: Plan next month thoughtfully
hook: Do more views always mean a more useful video?
message: Compare equal observation windows and qualified responses.
caption: Look beyond reach when reviewing what helped.
cta: Choose one question to test next month.

title: What we want to learn next
hook: What would make AI assistance worth trying for you?
message: Recap dispatcher-first education and both proposed concepts; invite qualified product questions to support awareness and potential-customer interest.
caption: ProfitLane is in development. Your judgment stays at the center.
cta: Follow @profitlane.dispatch for product updates. When a verified page and demo-request route exist, invite viewers to explore ProfitLane and request a demo.

title: A month of learning
hook: What should stay on the calendar next month?
message: Review actual results and choose useful next experiments.
caption: A thoughtful next month starts with what we learned.
cta: Suggest one topic for the next calendar.
